1.point: Because the soul is the instrument of all our knowing and the one thing we know directly, this chapter will show why and how knowing ourselves is the way to knowing our Lord.
steps: A familiar prayer confesses neglect of the soul (hook).
That confession implies the soul was given into our care and can be neglected.
The soul deserves that care because it is the instrument by which we understand everything.
It is also the one thing we know directly, by presence, not through an idea.
Knowing God, not merely about Him, needs that same direct knowing, so the chapter will set out why and how we must know ourselves to know our Lord.

2.point: The Qur'an makes the outcome of a human life turn on one thing, whether the soul is purified or betrayed, so the human story is the soul's story.
steps: Surah al-Shams closes its oaths with the soul and the discernment every soul is given.
The verses that follow make success and failure rest on what is done with that soul.
Therefore the whole human story is the story of the soul, and the Munajat's confession names the failure the surah describes.

3.point: God and the soul are forgotten together and known together, so knowing God starts with knowing the soul.
steps: Forgetting God causes forgetting the soul (al-Hashr).
So remembering God turns attention back to the soul, in stages.
The link also runs the other way: a ruined soul loses faith, a soul that is seen points to its Maker (al-Anʿam), because the soul is not assembled from parts.
Both directions are gathered in the saying 'whoever knows himself knows his Lord'.
The saying holds because the soul reflects its Maker (without being part of Him).
Hence knowing God begins with knowing the soul.

4.point: God is already present to us, so the distance is only a veil over our own soul, and the work of the path is to lift that veil now, not to wait for the meeting after death.
steps: We are already in God's presence; what we lack is perception of Him.
So the journey to Him covers no distance; it is the lifting of veils over the heart.
Every soul's veils come off at the promised meeting with God.
What is unveiled there is the soul, and seeing it unveiled is meeting God as reflected in it.
What a soul perceives of God then depends on what it perceives now (al-Isra): blindness carries over.
Therefore the veils must be lifted in this life, which is coming to know the soul and so the Lord.

¶1.label: advance
¶1.why: The hook: a prayer most readers know contains a confession, which the quotation then displays.

¶2.label: advance
¶2.why: Draws from the confession the first step: the soul is given into our care and can be neglected.

¶3.label: advance
¶3.why: Supplies why the soul deserves care: it is the instrument of all understanding. ¶5 uses this directly.

¶4.label: advance
¶4.why: Supplies the second ground, knowledge by presence: the soul is the one thing known directly. ¶5 and ¶23 depend on it.

¶5.label: advance
¶5.why: Draws the two grounds together and states what the chapter will establish, in the title's words. Its opening clause recaps ¶3-4, but the main claim is new.

¶6.label: advance
¶6.why: Sets up Surah al-Shams: the oath by the soul and the discernment every soul is given, which the displayed verses then build on.

¶7.label: advance
¶7.why: Draws from the verses the step the point needs: the outcome of a life rests on whether the soul is purified or betrayed.

¶8.label: advance
¶8.why: Draws the section's conclusion once (the human story is the soul's story) and closes the loop with the Munajat confession from ¶1-2.

¶9.label: advance
¶9.why: First link of the section: losing sight of the soul has a cause, forgetting God, named by al-Hashr.

¶10.label: aside
¶10.why: Widens the verse's scope to practising Muslims and softens it (not punishment, unrealised potential). Pastoral and true, but no later step uses it; the chain from ¶9 to ¶12 stands without it.

¶11.label: aside
¶11.why: A side remark on unrecognised sins and istighfar. Nothing later refers to it and the point (forgotten together, known together) does not need it.

¶12.label: advance
¶12.why: Supplies the God-to-soul direction of knowing: remembering God turns attention back to the soul, in stages.

¶13.label: advance
¶13.why: Supplies the new step that the link also runs from the soul to faith, introducing al-Anʿam.

¶14.label: support
¶14.why: Gives the reasoning ¶13's step needs: a soul that is seen points to its Maker because it is not assembled from parts. The closing sentence on chance theories is surplus within an otherwise needed paragraph.

¶15.label: advance
¶15.why: Joins the two directions ('so does knowing') and introduces the saying that the section's point rests on. Its first sentence summarises, but the gathering step is new.

¶16.label: support
¶16.why: Supplies the ground on which the saying holds, the soul reflects its Maker, and guards against reading it as pantheism. ¶22 and ¶27 reuse 'the soul reflects Him'.

¶17.label: advance
¶17.why: States the section's conclusion once, that knowing God begins with knowing the soul, and anchors the ordering in Tabatabaʾi's 'window of his own soul'.

¶18.label: advance
¶18.why: First link: we are already in God's presence; what is missing is our perception of Him.

¶19.label: advance
¶19.why: Draws the consequence: the journey covers no distance; it is the lifting of a veil over the heart. Introduces hijab, which the point turns on.

¶20.label: advance
¶20.why: Supplies the step that for every soul the veils come off at the promised meeting, setting up the contrast with lifting them now.

¶21.label: support
¶21.why: Glosses the verse and gives the lecture's words that at the meeting the layers over the soul are removed, which ¶22 builds on. Its first two sentences repeat ¶20.

¶22.label: advance
¶22.why: Supplies the link between 'meeting God' and 'seeing one's own soul': the soul is a reflection of God, so an unveiled soul is the meeting. The believer/unbeliever mercy/justice sentence is surplus.

¶23.label: aside
¶23.why: A qualification: even unveiled, the soul gives no complete knowledge of God. True, but nothing later uses it; ¶25 moves straight on. Cutting it leaves no step unsupported.

¶24.label: restate
¶24.why: Announces itself as 'the same line' as ¶23 and ends on the same claim (nearness, never a grasp). A second scholar saying what ¶23 said. Its one new and useful element, that the meeting is open to the seeker in this life, is buried and not used.

¶25.label: advance
¶25.why: Supplies the decisive step: what a soul perceives at the meeting depends on what it perceives now, via al-Isra.

¶26.label: advance
¶26.why: Draws the conclusion once: blindness carries over, so the veils must be lifted now. The Tabrizi sentences tie veil-lifting to the saying from ¶15, which ¶27 leans on.

¶27.label: restate
¶27.why: A summary: God is near (¶18), the soul reflects Him (¶16), a veil over the soul keeps us from Him (¶19), lifting it is knowing the soul and the Lord (¶26). Every claim already made; the conclusion is stated a second time.

¶28.label: aside
¶28.why: A bridge question to the next chapter that this section does not answer. It adds no link to the point.
